// Vehicle Breakdown — Best Years · Engines · What To Avoid
K5 Blazer / GMC Jimmy
Chevy · GMC  |  Square Body: 1973–1991
SBC 350 V8
1973–1977
CautionEarly emissions equipment — EGR valves and air pumps are annoying but deletable. Mechanically pure underneath. Worth it if body and frame are solid.
1978–1979
Sweet SpotPre-computer simplicity at its peak. Pure carb, no electronics, mechanical everything. Hardest to find in your market but the cleanest wrenching experience.
1980–1982
AvoidGM's Computer Command Control transition era. Worst of both worlds — not simple enough to be pure, not reliable enough to be modern. Electronic carb is a headache.
1983–1986
Target WindowElectronics settled down. Still carbureted — fundamentally understandable. Most common in Charleston market at your budget. 350 four-barrel is well sorted. Best entry point.
1987–1991
Also GreatTBI fuel injection — two injectors where the carb was. More reliable in Charleston heat, starts perfectly every time. The 1991 is the most refined square body ever made.
// Notes

350 small block + TH350/TH400 is the most documented engine combo in the hobby. Every problem solved publicly. Parts at NAPA tomorrow.

Largest rear tub in this category. Longboard fits diagonally with tailgate down and rear window slid open.

Soft top aftermarket is the most developed of any vehicle on this list — Softopper and others have direct-fit solutions.

Best Year: 1991
Best Budget: 1983–86
Avoid: 1980–82
Parts: Easiest on list
Full-Size Bronco
Ford  |  Full-Size Run: 1978–1996
351W / 5.0 / 5.8
1978–1979
Good351 Windsor or 400 V8. Pre-computer simplicity. Harder to find but worth hunting if pre-1980 is the priority.
1980–1984
AvoidFord's feedback carburetor system is genuinely awful — worse than GM's equivalent. Complex, unreliable, hard to diagnose. Pass unless carb has been converted out.
1985–1991
Sweet SpotEFI from 1986 onward and it's actually excellent. 5.0 and 5.8 Windsor are reliable and very wrenchable. Strong parts support. Good daily viability.
1992–1996
Most RefinedMost sorted and reliable generation. Best daily driver of the run. Last year (1996) commands a premium. Getting more expensive but most usable.
// Notes

Ford community is strong but a tier below the Chevy ecosystem. More online ordering, less NAPA walk-in.

Rear tub is notably smaller than the K5 — longboard situation is tighter. Verify against your actual board before committing.

The 1980–84 feedback carb era is likely why many Charleston examples are cheap. Budget for a carb conversion if buying in that window.

Best Years: 1985–91
Avoid: 1980–84
Parts: Good, Ford ecosystem
Ramcharger
Dodge  |  Run: 1974–1993
318 / 360 V8
1974–1978
GoodPre lean-burn. Simple and honest. The 360 V8 is straightforward and torquey. Best pure wrenching experience of the Ramcharger run.
1979–1983
AvoidChrysler's Electronic Lean Burn ignition is the single worst thing about this era. Notoriously hard to diagnose. Verify it has been converted to standard ignition before buying anything in this window.
1984–1993
SortedLean burn gone. Electronics settled. 318 and 360 are reliable and underrated. Genuinely fine to own and wrench on. Cheapest entry point of the three full-size options right now.
// Notes

Smallest community of the three. More online ordering, less walk-in parts availability. Not a dealbreaker — just a reality to plan around.

Same physical size class as the K5 — rear tub is comparable. Longboard solution works similarly.

Sleeper value play — prices have not followed the K5 and Bronco trajectory yet. The "nobody else has one" factor is real.

Best Years: 1984–93
Avoid: 1979–83 lean burn
Value: Best price/size right now
1st Gen 4Runner
Toyota  |  Removable Top Years: 1984–1989
22RE I4
1984–1985
Early BuildFirst production years. Some early quirks being sorted. Still fine but later years are more refined. Rarest and most collectible — prices reflect it.
1986–1987
Sweet SpotEarly issues resolved. 22RE fully sorted. Best combination of simplicity and reliability in the run. Clean SE example in this window is a buy.
1988–1989
Most AvailableMost produced years. Best chance of finding a solid example in your market. Last year (1989) before the 2nd gen enclosed body. Slightly more refined interior.
// Notes

The 22RE is arguably the most reliable engine on this entire list. Nearly unbreakable with basic maintenance. One weakness: head gasket failure caused almost exclusively by prior overheating — always get cooling system history.

Take the 4-cylinder. The V6 (3VZ-E) has a well-documented head gasket problem and is not worth the risk.

Manual transmission is actually findable on these — unlike the American alternatives. The manual 22RE combo is deeply satisfying.

Frame rails and removable top condition are the two things to check first. Budget $10–14k for anything genuinely solid. Under $8k needs careful scrutiny.

Best Years: 1986–89
Engine: 22RE only — skip V6
Manual: Findable
Budget: $10–14k solid
// Universal Inspection Checklist — Every Candidate
// Frame First

Get underneath with a flashlight before you start the engine. Poke frame rails with a screwdriver — should feel like steel. Soft or crumbly = walk away, full stop.

// Floor Pans

Lift the carpet. Look for rust-through. Coastal humidity accelerates this even without road salt. Repairable but factor cost into your offer.

// Top Mounts

Check soft top mounting points and hardware condition. UV damage on coastal vehicles is real. Replacement tops are available but the structure needs to be sound.

// Transfer Case

Engage 4WD and verify it shifts in and out cleanly. Listen for whining from rear differential. These are expensive fixes if they've been neglected.

// Cooling History

Ask about overheating history on every engine — especially the 22RE and any V6. Head gasket failures are almost always caused by prior overheating events.

// Lifted = Caution

Lifted examples with big tires are often abused examples. Verify drivetrain was maintained. A stock-height solid example beats a lifted mystery every time.
